sentences.text: Lee Whitfield (client) attended the meeting with Sophie Grant (solicitor) to discuss housing arrears and other debts.
Lee Whitfield lost his job at the depot in January.
Lee Whitfield described the Universal Credit housing element as 'going wrong', causing rent to build up.
Lee Whitfield stated the rent arrears are £3,850, potentially covering three or four months.
Lee Whitfield has court papers for a hearing on the 9th of December at Harbridge County Court.
The court papers are a possession claim on rent arrears grounds (ground eight, ten and eleven) by Ashcroft Lettings.
Lee Whitfield has lived at the private property for six years.
Lee Whitfield lives alone with a cat.
Lee Whitfield offered £50 a month in September; the landlord rejected this and demanded full payment.
Lee Whitfield has the landlord's rejection offer in writing as a text message on his phone.
Lee Whitfield reported damp in the bedroom ('black up the wall') and stated he has told the landlord about it and has photos.
Lee Whitfield has outstanding debts for council tax (bailiffs letter received), a credit card debt of about £2,000, and electricity on a meter.
Lee Whitfield has no support for the debts and has stopped opening mail.
Lee Whitfield reported taking an overdose of 16 paracetamol in March after receiving the first rent arrears letter; he was found by a neighbour, kept in hospital overnight, and had
Lee Whitfield reported that in March he thought about ending his life on Sunday night but did not act on it.
Lee Whitfield stated he is safe today and has not hurt himself since March.
Lee Whitfield reported he put the housing problem on his Universal Credit journal twice with no answer.
Lee Whitfield stated he felt a bit better after the meeting.
Lee Whitfield stated he has the tenancy agreement, rent statement, Universal Credit statements since January, and damp photos.
Lee Whitfield offered to email the documents by Friday the 27th.
Lee Whitfield expressed a wish to have his GP see him today.
Lee Whitfield requested to ring his GP together with the solicitor.
Lee Whitfield requested the crisis team number and Samaritans (116 123).
Lee Whitfield stated he might not lose the flat due to the defence and potential counterclaim for damp.
Lee Whitfield expressed a desire for a 'breathing space' from creditors for 60 days.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised that Lee Whitfield has a defence regarding the arrears and the damp could be a counterclaim to reduce the debt.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would file a defence and counterclaim.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would ask the court to adjourn if more time is needed to sort the Universal Credit.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would refer Lee Whitfield to the Citizens Advice debt team for a 60-day breathing space.
Solicitor Sophie Grant advised she would write to Universal Credit regarding the housing problem as part of the defence.
